analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one benchmark table row at head line 572 for a `--prompt-prep` harness. The row describes a CPU-only mode that loads only the tokenizer, prints JSON, and exits 2 on any token-ID or decoded-field difference. This is documentation only, so there are no code, authorization, attestation, encryption, or billing changes. I checked the new row against the threat model. The mode loads no model weights and no KEK. It does not touch TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket), TB-011, A-003 or A-016. It does not touch the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041), because the description says it times a prompt token cache with background comparisons off and says nothing about the on-disk KV tier. The description of a 'prompt token cache' is a different component from the T-041 SSD prefix cache, so it neither widens nor narrows the T-041 at-rest surface. No finding is raised. A remaining integration question is whether the new `PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift` and any prompt token cache it exercises (a separate source change, not supplied here) persist prompt-derived data to disk or share it across tenants. If so, T-041 would need a fresh review. Nothing in the supplied text establishes that. Unchanged lines 1-830 of the file were read for context and show no new security claims.
